issues: All original 1647 claims about eyesight, hearing, speech, teeth, seizures, psychiatric labels, urinary stones, gout and violent falls are unsupported period medical hypotheses, never clinical evidence.
Several short original author-claimed rules say a person 'shall be blind', 'deaf' or epileptic; none can inform real-person diagnosis, safety or treatment.
No actual patients, verified birth-time sources, medical records, appropriate comparison controls or longitudinal events are presented by the author.
Named zodiac ranges for Milky Way, Pleiades, Praesepe, Coma Berenices, Cor Scorpio, Orion and cloudy fixed stars require historically correct star identities and epoch coordinates.
Several planetary/zodiac glyphs, conjunction and opposition operators in the eye and neurological paragraphs remain unresolved pending diplomatic first-edition transcription and mathematical review.
Sun-right/Moon-left eye laterality reflects period interpretation, not clinically validated human visual anatomy.
The author's suggested cause of eye injury by Saturn catarrh or Mars trauma is speculative astrological attribution, not actual etiology.
The eye section includes total blindness, one-eye injury and squint, and contradictory conditions with and without angular malefics.
The hearing section offers several sixth, eighth, tenth, Ascendant, Saturn/Mercury alternatives and explicitly allows benefic mitigation. No validated diagnosis or outcome matching exists.
The speech section treats stammering, muteness and disability through compound Mercury/mute-sign conditions; no clinical neurodevelopmental association is demonstrated.
Dental pain, loss and alleged elemental causes are separate outcomes with contrary air/earth/fire branches; no real dental chart histories supplied.
Falling-sickness, epilepsy, seizure, madness, foolery and intellectual disability are conflated under premodern stigmatizing categories. Do not use them as modern psychiatric or neurologic diagnoses.
The four supposedly epileptic causes are attributed to Albubater, Cardanus and Pontanus, not validated external clinical findings.
The four-sect combinations of Moon/Mercury/Saturn/Mars have ambiguous grammatical conjunction scope and sign labels.
Stone/strangury and gout combinations are compound physical disease claims with many alternative planet, house, aspect and sign outcomes.
Gout is claimed to follow youth sickness at unspecified later ages; no objective age interval, severity or case count.
Violent fall predictions invoke fixed stars, horses or beasts and house-specific malefics, and Lilly cites his own unverifiable experiences.
The subheadings for ears, tongue, tooth, falling sickness, stone, gout and falls are all within printed CXXVIII; they do not increment numbered-chapter coverage.
Printed CHAP CXXIX on whether disease is curable begins lower original PDF619; printed CXXX on servants and small cattle begins original PDF620 and neither is substantive source accepted here.
This corpus is an anchored selective semantic documentary extraction, not full diplomatic transcription or proof of predictive astrological performance.
